info.name: Project Task Management API
info.description: Full REST API collection for the Project & Task Management System (Auth, Users, Projects, Tasks, Comments, Dashboard). Import the companion environment (ProjectTaskManagement.postman_environment.json), then run the requests inside 'Auth > Login as Admin' (or Manager/Developer) first — it auto-saves the access/refresh tokens used by every other request. Requests that create a resource (Create Project, Create Task, Create Comment) auto-save the new id for use by later requests in the same folder.

request.description: Self-registration always creates a Developer, regardless of any role field sent.
Rotating refresh: the old token is revoked and a new pair issued. Re-using an already-rotated token returns 401 and revokes the whole family.

Revokes all of the caller's refresh tokens on success. The example currentPassword is deliberately a placeholder that won't match any seeded account, so running this as-is safely 409s instead of silently changing the shared demo Admin's password — replace it with your real current password before running for real.
409 if targeting yourself — Admins cannot change their own role.
409 if targeting yourself. Deactivating invalidates that user's existing access tokens immediately.
Admin or Manager only. Manager becomes owner automatically; Admin may pass an explicit `owner`.
Auto-scoped by role: Admin sees all, Manager sees owned + member-of, Developer sees member-of only.
Legal transitions only: Planning->In Progress, In Progress->Completed/Planning, Completed->In Progress. Illegal jumps (e.g. Planning->Completed) return 409.
Must be active Developers. Idempotent — adding an existing member again is a no-op, not an error.

query.description: Required if the member has open tasks in this project — otherwise this returns 409.

request.description: Same filter set as GET /tasks (status, priority, assignee, dueDateFrom/To, overdue, search), pre-scoped to this project.

body.raw:

  "title": "Postman Demo Task",
  "description": "Created from the Postman collection.",
  "project": "{{projectId}}",
  "priority": "P2",
  "dueDate": "2026-12-01"
}

request.description: Admin, or Manager on their own project. 409 if the project is Completed.
Auto-scoped by role, same as GET /projects.
dueDate < now AND status != Done AND not deleted — computed in the query, never in JS after fetching.
title/description/priority/dueDate only — reassignment has its own endpoint. Admin, or Manager on their own project.

Admin/Manager(own project), or a Developer on their own assigned task. Legal transitions: Todo->In Progress->Review->Done, with Review->In Progress and In Progress->Todo and Done->In Progress also allowed. Illegal jumps return 409.
assignee must be the project owner or a member — 400 otherwise. Pass null to unassign.
Any project member (including the owner). 403 for non-members.
Author only (Admin may edit any).
Author or Admin. Soft delete, 204.
Cached (see X-Cache response header: MISS then HIT on the next call within the TTL). Role-scoped: org-wide for Admin, owned/member projects for Manager, assigned tasks for Developer.
Admin and Manager only — a Developer gets 403.

item.name: Error Scenarios
item.description: Representative failure cases for the four error statuses the API documents (400/401/403/404/409). Run 'Auth > Login as Developer' before the 403 examples.

item.name: Setup: create scratch project (as Admin, for the 409 example)

request.description: Always starts in Planning, independent of whatever the Projects folder left {{projectId}} as.
Missing required 'name' — expect { statusCode: 400, message: 'Validation failed', details: [...] }.
A malformed ObjectId returns 400, never a raw 500.
Run 'Auth > Login as Developer' first. Project creation is Admin/Manager only.
Scratch project is fresh from setup (Planning), so Planning -> Completed is illegal and must 409.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Run last — deletes the resources the earlier folders created.

request.description: Soft delete, 204. Admin or Manager(own project) only — a Developer gets 403 even on their own assigned task.
Soft delete — cascades to the project's tasks and their comments. Returns 204. Run this last, or against a throwaway project.
